Connor  0:03
I keep thinking about how I take notes in meetings and never read them again.
I fill a notebook every month and I could not tell you one thing from the March notebook.

Priya  0:15
That's because notes are for remembering during the meeting, not after it.
If you wrote down only decisions and owners, you would actually read them.

Connor  0:27
Maybe. Or maybe I should stop taking notes and just write a summary at the end.
Three lines, what we decided, who owns it, when we check again.

Priya  0:40
That's the same idea as the decision log your team tried last year, isn't it?
Why did that one die?

Connor  0:47
Because nobody owned the log. It was everyone's job, which meant it was nobody's job.
If one person owns the summary each week, it might survive. I want to try that this month.
And if it dies again, at least we will know the reason was not the format, it was the ownership.
